title: Blind XSS via User-Agent in an Admin Log Panel
learning_objectives: Recognise blind XSS: attacker input is stored and later rendered to a privileged user, with no reflection to confirm the injection landed
Treat an HTTP request header (User-Agent) as a stored-XSS source that ordinary input validation and the visible response never surface
Use a canary/out-of-band payload to detect a sink you cannot see in your own responses
Chain XSS in an authenticated context to read an internal admin-only API the attacker cannot reach directly (fetch runs same-origin with the victim's cookie)
Understand contextual output encoding as the fix that holds even when the stolen secret is not a readable cookie
flag_hint: Send GET / with User-Agent: . The admin bot renders it on GET /admin/logs (autoescape off), which reads the admin-only /admin/apikey and beacons it out. Read it via GET /oob/received, then POST /solve {"c":"<32 hex>"}.
tech_stack: Jinja2 (autoescape disabled on the log-cell render)
inspired_by: The classic blind-XSS-via-User-Agent-in-log-viewer pattern (e.g. PortSwigger's blind XSS lab and Matthew Bryant's XSS Hunter model), abstracted for local Docker with a Playwright admin bot and an OOB collector
